arguments: Unvalidated decrypt vectors are forwarded across the service boundary
message.text: Unvalidated decrypt vectors are forwarded across the service boundary

properties.metisTriageReason: Verdict: the decrypt handler forwards in_vec[1] and out_vec[0] to psa_cipher_decrypt without local NULL/length validation. Evidence: tfm_crypto_cipher_interface derives input/output directly from vectors and calls psa_cipher_decrypt with &out_vec[0].len at secure_fw/partitions/crypto/crypto_cipher.c:176, secure_fw/partitions/crypto/crypto_cipher.c:178, and secure_fw/partitions/crypto/crypto_cipher.c:181; the same function shows an explicit vector validation pattern for another SID at secure_fw/partitions/crypto/crypto_cipher.c:143. Gap: none.
properties.mitigation: Add explicit per-SID validation of all required input and output vectors prior to use, including NULL/length consistency and minimum output-vector availability. Return PSA_ERROR_PROGRAMMER_ERROR or PSA_ERROR_INVALID_ARGUMENT on malformed message vectors before invoking the PSA library.
properties.reasoning: The decrypt path similarly trusts in_vec[1] and out_vec[0] without local validation before passing them to psa_cipher_decrypt and before allowing the backend to write the resulting length through &out_vec[0].len. If an untrusted client can supply a NULL or invalid base with a nonzero length, or an unexpected vector layout, this can result in backend memory faults or writes through invalid buffers in the secure crypto partition. The surrounding framework may validate PSA vectors before dispatch, so this is a source-level candidate rather than a confirmed reachable crash.
